`public/models/helmet.glb` is now a 1024px KTX2 version. It uses **7 MiB of GPU memory**, down from **107 MiB**, and scores 0.940 fidelity against the original.

| Candidate | GPU MiB | File size | Fidelity | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original JPEG 2048 | 107 | 3.77 MB | 1.00 | baseline |
| Default recipe (WebP 2048) | 107 | 3.10 MB | 0.959 | no GPU saving |
| WebP 1024 | 27 | 1.23 MB | 0.879 | below floor |
| KTX2 2048 | not measured | 10.5 MB | — | larger file, not needed |
| KTX2 1536 | 15.4 | 6.67 MB | not measured | not needed |
| KTX2 1024, ETC1S only | 7 | 0.97 MB | 0.748 | below floor |
| KTX2 1024, UASTC only | 7 | 4.39 MB | 0.944 | same quality, bigger file |
| **KTX2 1024, default ETC1S+UASTC** | **7** | **3.29 MB** | **0.940** | **chosen** |
| KTX2 512 | 2 | 1.23 MB | 0.782 | below floor |

Fidelity is `node-assets`' worst-region SSIM over four 1024px views. Its recommended floor for no visible quality loss is 0.90. The chosen version sits above that with some margin, and 512px and the ETC1S-only version fall well below it.

What the change involves:
- **Decoder:** the file needs the KTX2 transcoder (`KHR_texture_basisu`). Babylon.js loads it automatically, as you said. Anything else loading this file would need `KTX2Loader` set up.
- **Geometry:** unchanged in the default recipe, at 15,452 triangles. Geometry was not the GPU cost, so I didn't simplify it.
- **Load time:** this is not faster in headless Chromium. Cold KTX2 transcoding made the load about 4.9 s versus 4.3–5.5 s for the original. The gain is GPU memory, not load time.

The candidate files are in `/tmp/claude-0/helmet-cand/`, outside the repo. Nothing else in `public/` or `assets/` was changed.
